label: Past of a moment with a beginning
definition: BegunAt t holds when some moment m at or before t (m = t or m < t) has no strictly earlier moment: the past of t has a minimal moment, which in linear time is its first moment. In a branching order other branches below t may still descend without end; one minimal moment suffices. Discrete time with a first moment and continuous time with a first moment both give every moment a begun past (checked for non-negative rationals in BegunComingToBe.controls). An endless discrete past (integer time) and an open-below continuous past (no first moment) give no moment a begun past.
note: Analyst framework definition; attribution deferred. Weaker than a founded past (Acc of the strict order): a founded past has a beginning (begunOfAcc), but continuous time with a first moment gives later moments a begun past that is not founded, since t, t/2, t/4, … descend endlessly below t (checked for non-negative rationals). A begun past is not a finite past: infinitely many moments may lie between the beginning and t. The beginning is a minimal moment of the supplied time order, not a first event, cause or state, and says nothing about what is present at it.
